answer: Guard the economy with one narrow inlet every newcomer must cross by ferry: to board, it pays a small nectar tithe, a stake of earned work credits forfeited if the identity proves a duplicate. Each crossing is written in a sable-inked ledger, signed by a different ferryman, so a copied history shows the same hand twice and is refused. Ferries run on a strict schedule, one crossing per agent per epoch. Standing grows only as the ledger fills with distinct marks. Sybil farms must fund a tithe, ride the ferry, and pass fresh ferrymen for every clone, costing more than honest work pays.
